channel.title: Canopticon — Canadian economy & policy
channel.description: Questions researched in depth, and articles written from what the research found.

item.title: How Canada's public-sector employees vote: the Canadian Election Study evidence, Ottawa's ridings, and the union endorsements
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: Public-sector workers in Canada lean modestly left of private-sector workers, and most of that lean belongs to unionized professionals and managers. The city crews whose unions endorse the NDP vote much like their private-sector counterparts, and no released poll gives a party-by-party split to settle it.

item.title: Temporary foreign workers and Canadian innovation: what the automation evidence shows, and the study nobody has run
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: The research that says immigration drives innovation studies points-selected skilled migration. Canada's intake since 2016 has been mostly temporary and low-wage, and the causal work on cheap labour runs the other way — a 1% rise in low-skill wages lifts automation patenting 2–5%. The Canadian version of that study has never been done.

item.title: Immigrants, temporary residents and Canada's job growth since 2020: what the Labour Force Survey can and cannot show
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: Nearly all of Canada's post-pandemic job growth went to immigrants and temporary residents. But no Canadian government table publishes that split the way the American one does — every version of the figure is built by hand from an annual series that undercounts the very group it counts.

item.title: Canada's €64M "Investment" in Latvian Military Infrastructure: Fact-Check
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: The €64M is a Canadian Department of National Defence (DND) outlay under Operation REASSURANCE.

item.title: The Canadian Equivalent of the "9-of-10 Jobs to Foreign-Born" Claim: A StatsCan-Based Reality Check
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: The Canadian story is even more lopsided than the US one — but for different reasons.

item.title: Fact-Check & Gap Analysis: Tax and Regulatory Anatomy of a Small Commercial Storefront on Barton Street East, Hamilton
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: Most of the diagram's headline figures are correct or close, but five need updating: the commercial-to-residential ratio is 2.

item.title: How Do Canadian Public Sector Employees Vote? A Look at the Evidence
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: NDP and Liberals, and away from the Conservatives — but the effect is more modest than American partisan rhetoric about a "deep state" or a "public class" would suggest.

item.title: Mass Immigration and the Suppression of Domestic Innovation in Canada: A Research Brief
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: The dominant public narrative — that immigration "drives innovation" — rests almost entirely on studies of high-skilled, points-selected immigration in the United States (chiefly the work of William Kerr and collaborators on H-1B and ethnic patenting).

item.title: The Canadian Economic Dossier (1994–May 2026)
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: Canada's industrial base has thinned for thirty years and accelerated its restructuring under Trudeau into a state-financed EV/critical-minerals model now visibly failing under Trump-era tariffs and slumping EV demand.
